bull.b: The sharp FY2026 recovery in revenue and profitability, together with multi-year gross-margin improvement, indicates stronger pricing, mix, or cost execution. Higher margins create greater capacity to reinvest in brands and stores while supporting more durable earnings power.

Robust operating and free cash flow provides internal funding for growth investments, technology, and stores while supporting dividends and repurchases. Cash conversion that broadly follows earnings also strengthens confidence that reported profitability is backed by real cash generation.

Coach is demonstrating meaningful international and regional momentum, while broad customer acquisition expands the future addressable base. Gen Z customers reportedly show higher AURs and stronger retention, potentially supporting repeat purchases and long-term brand relevance.

bear.b: The substantially higher leverage makes shareholder outcomes more sensitive to any earnings downturn and reduces financial flexibility. A thinner equity base can amplify returns when performance is strong, but also raises refinancing and balance-sheet pressure if cash generation weakens.

bear.t: Kate Spade revenue and profit weakness
bear.b: Kate Spade remains a meaningful portfolio drag because declining sales and an expected operating loss can offset Coach's growth and constrain consolidated margin expansion. The brand requires continued investment before management expects a return to sustainable top-line growth.

The expected deceleration through FY2027 reduces visibility into a consistently accelerating revenue base. Uneven growth can make operating leverage and cash-flow forecasting less reliable, particularly when the company is also managing investment levels and brand-specific performance differences.
